surface-deep.purpose: Ladder rung 1 — hero band and brand statement band.

surface-dark.purpose: Ladder rung 2 — programmes band and footer plate.

surface-dark-raised.purpose: Ladder rung 3 — cards and media wells sitting on a dark band, never a band itself.

surface-bright.purpose: Ladder rung 5 — default section ground and every light card or control fill.

on-dark-1.purpose: Headings, episode and programme names on dark. 19.1:1 deep / 15.4:1 dark / 13.5:1 raised.

on-dark-2.purpose: Descriptions and footer column heads on dark. 11.8 / 9.5 / 8.3.

on-dark-3.purpose: Metadata and quiet actions on dark; the floor on --surface-dark-raised. 6.5 / 5.2 / 4.6.

on-dark-4.purpose: Inactive and utility text on the two dark bands ONLY. 5.7 deep / 4.6 dark / 4.0 raised (fails).

on-light-1.purpose: Headings and card titles on light. 17.6:1 white / 15.7:1 archive band.

on-light-2.purpose: Descriptions and prose on light. 7.9:1 white / 7.1:1 archive band.

on-light-3.purpose: Metadata on light; the AA floor. 5.5:1 white / 4.9:1 archive band.

accent.purpose: Play, CTA, active state, progress, focus. Never a surface, never body text.

accent-pressed.purpose: Hover / pressed step under any gold fill; input caret. Reached in the build via --gold-deep.

accent-on-light.purpose: The gold family darkened to AA as text on paper. Declared, currently unreferenced — it exists so gold text on light never uses raw gold.

border-dark.purpose: Every 1px rule on a dark surface, including the statement/footer seam.

border-light.purpose: Every 1px rule on a light surface — section heads, pick rows.

display.purpose: The brand statement band only — the brand speaking in its own voice.

h1.purpose: The hero episode title overlaying the poster; balanced wrap.

h2.purpose: Every section head across the site.

h3.purpose: Programme card title on the programmes page and the picks lead.

body-lg.purpose: Lead paragraphs, long-form prose (line-height 2–2.1, 70–72ch), hero CTA label.

body.purpose: Episode card titles (700/1.55) and default copy; body base is 16px/1.7.

body-sm.purpose: Buttons, nav links, programme descriptions, compact pick rows.

meta.purpose: Dates, durations, counts, chips, tags, selects, footer base — the most-used token in the system.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, filmstrip label, duration badges, footer column heads, filter badge.

shadows.name: sh-1
shadows.purpose: Resting episode thumb on light; active segmented pill; contact-card hover.

shadows.name: sh-2
shadows.purpose: Episode thumb on hover, picks lead thumb, toast, next-card lift.

shadows.name: sh-navy
shadows.purpose: The cinematic shadow — hero stage, player, programme hero cover.

shadows.name: disc-rest
shadows.purpose: The 84px gold play disc at rest on the hero stage.

shadows.name: disc-hover
shadows.purpose: The same disc on hover, paired with scale(1.07).

shadows.name: btn-gold
shadows.purpose: Seats the gold button on dark media without a border.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Mobile filter sheet rising over the page.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the system.

motion.name: t-med
motion.purpose: Overlays, underlines, lifts, the programme rule and arrow fill.

motion.name: t-slow
motion.purpose: Media scale, crossfades, the programme artwork bleed.

motion.name: strip-secs
motion.purpose: Signature filmstrip auto-advance interval; also drives the CSS progress hairline.

motion.name: stage-swap
motion.purpose: Delay before the hero stage re-renders during a crossfade (info fades over 240ms).

adjacentSeparation.where: statement → footer — the tightest pair; the seam also carries a border-dark hairline
card on a dark band — separates by radius and padding, gains a hairline on hover
the two light rungs — never placed adjacent

narrative.overview:
A permanent Arabic archive that feels like a premium broadcaster's vault, not a news portal. The site is built from full-width bands, and the bands are the design: a five-rung surface ladder runs from near-black cinema through to paper, and a page is composed by stepping along it so that no two neighbouring bands can ever visually merge. Deep rungs carry video and brand ceremony; bright rungs carry reading and browsing; one gold voice points at everything playable.

The system is now two-layered. A raw palette (navy scale, gold family, paper/ink/line) names the pigments; a semantic layer on top names the jobs — surfaces, text steps, borders, accent — and every value in it was chosen against two tests at once: adjacent bands must separate, and the text steps must clear 4.5:1 on each band they are allowed to sit on. New components address the semantic layer only.

Density is editorial: 104px band rhythm, 16:9 media everywhere, 1px rules instead of boxes, a five-step radius scale, restrained shadows. Every thumbnail is an authored inline-SVG poster generated per programme — the site never shows a stock image or a grey placeholder. Confirmed rejections (pinned in PRODUCT.md, honoured by the build): no SaaS genericity, no heavy gradients or glassmorphism, no childish cards, no extreme rounding, no colourful multi-hue UI.
keyCharacteristics: A five-rung surface ladder with measured adjacent separation, not a two-tone navy/white alternation.
A semantic token layer over the raw palette; components speak semantics.
Text steps audited per surface — every text/surface pair in the build passes AA (4.5:1).
Noto Kufi Arabic display over IBM Plex Sans Arabic body, both on a nine-step size scale.
Authored per-programme SVG poster system (7 motifs, seeded variation, Arabic-Indic numerals).
One signature auto-motion (hero filmstrip); everything else moves only in response to input.
RTL-first: logical properties only, LTR islands only where the content demands one.
Fully data-driven: header, footer, cards and pages render from data.js through app.js.

rules.name: The Semantic-Only Rule
rules.body: New components address the semantic layer — --surface-*, --on-dark-*, --on-light-*, --border-*, --accent*. The raw palette exists to define those tokens and nothing else. The refactored surfaces (hero, latest, programme index, archive, statement, footer, episode cards, section heads) already obey this; the light chrome and the interior page heroes still address the raw palette and should be migrated as they are next touched. Do not add new raw-palette references.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: Every band declares one rung of the surface ladder, and two adjacent bands may never share a rung. The homepage reads deep → bright → dark → light → deep → dark. Where the ladder alone is too tight — statement → footer at 1.24:1 — the seam must also carry a hairline (border-block-start: 1px solid var(--border-dark) on the footer). No gradient ever transitions one band into another.

rules.name: The Raised-Surface Floor Rule
rules.body: --on-dark-4 is legal only on the two dark bands (--surface-deep 5.7:1, --surface-dark 4.6:1). Anything sitting on --surface-dark-raised steps up to --on-dark-3, because -4 falls to 4.0:1 there. Text is never placed on a surface it was not audited against.

rules.name: The Yellow Points Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only where attention or action lives: play, CTA, active state, progress, focus. It never fills a band, never sets body text, and never labels a category. One gold action per view region. If a screen reads 'gold' at a glance, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Kufi Voice Rule
rules.body: Noto Kufi Arabic appears only on headings, programme and card titles, big poster numerals and the mobile nav links — always 600–800. Everything else is IBM Plex Sans Arabic. Arabic line-heights stay generous (headings ≥1.35, hero and statement 1.4–1.5); Latin-tight leading clips Arabic ascenders.

rules.name: The Scale Rule
rules.body: Component type comes from the nine --t-* tokens. A literal font-size is permitted only for a page-level h1 clamp or the programme-index name; anything else that needs a size the scale does not have is a sign the scale is being avoided.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every count, date and duration sets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. Dates render through Intl.DateTimeFormat('ar-EG', …); standalone numbers convert through arNum() to ٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩. Durations, handles and URLs are LTR islands — .ltr-num (direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate), .thumb-dur { direction: ltr }, contact handles unicode-bidi: plaintext.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Separation defaults to a 1px rule — --border-light on paper, --border-dark on dark. A shadow is earned only by media (sh-navy), by a light card at rest (sh-1), or by something floating above the page (toast, sheet, hover lift).

dos: Do build every new band from a surface-ladder rung, and check the pair above and below it: if two neighbours land within ~1.3:1, the seam also needs a --border-dark hairline (the statement→footer pair at 1.24:1 is the worked example).
Do address the semantic layer — --surface-*, --on-dark-*, --on-light-*, --border-*, --accent* — in every new component, and migrate raw-palette references when you touch old ones.
Do step text up to --on-dark-3 on anything sitting on --surface-dark-raised; --on-dark-4 belongs to the two dark bands only.
Do take component type from the nine --t-* tokens and spacing from the six --sp-* tokens.
Do keep hover effects on the compositor: animate opacity and transform only. The programme index's artwork is deliberately fixed-width for this reason.
Do write CSS with logical properties only, give every grid child min-width: 0, and put direction: ltr on any inline SVG containing text and on any mm:ss / URL / handle inside the RTL page.
Do render numerals Arabic-Indic (arNum() / ar-EG dates) with tabular-nums, and draw icons from the sprite at stroke 1.75.
Do bump ?v=N on every CSS/JS reference across all seven pages together on every asset change (currently ?v=24).
Do start dark-hero pages with data-header="dark" and light pages with data-header="light".
donts: Don't place two bands of the same rung next to each other, or fade one band into another with a gradient — the only gradients are media scrims, the programme-index mask, and the programme hero's radial tint.
Don't put text on a surface it was not audited against, and never introduce a fourth muted step to 'fit' a contrast problem — restructure the surface instead.
Don't use gold as a surface, as body text, or on more than one action per region; gold text on a light surface steps down to --accent-on-light.
Don't give the episode card a programme badge, a coloured chip, or a bullet glyph — thumbnail, title, then one muted 'programme · date' line is the whole hierarchy.
Don't let a second element compete with the hero's play disc: .stage-info stays capped at ~54% and the disc stays offset into the free half of the frame.

Don't animate width, height, top/left or any layout property on hover; and don't add a second self-moving element — the filmstrip is the only one, and anything new must obey the same pause / coarse-pointer / reduced-motion discipline.
Don't exceed the five-step radius scale; the only off-scale values are 50% for circles and 0 for a deliberate reset.
Don't introduce raster thumbnails, stock photography or icon fonts — posters are generated SVG, icons are the authored sprite.
Don't hand-write card or page markup in HTML; extend the app.js renderers and the data.js schema so a CMS swap stays possible.
Don't animate cards in on scroll — reveals belong to section heads only.
